items.value: The region along the eastern Mediterranean shores
items.reasoning: The Levant is the historical name for the lands at the eastern end of the Mediterranean — broadly Syria, Lebanon, Israel, Palestine, Jordan and adjoining parts of Turkey, with Cyprus often included. The word itself comes from the French for 'rising', meaning the direction of sunrise as seen from Western Europe. The North African coast from Egypt to Morocco is the Maghreb, not the Levant, and neither the Persian Gulf nor the entire Mediterranean rim answers to the term.

items.value: Only Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan border Afghanistan
items.reasoning: Afghanistan's neighbours are Iran to the west, Pakistan to the south and east, China at the eastern tip of the Wakhan Corridor, and three Central Asian republics to the north — Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan, the last three separated from it largely by the Amu Darya. Kyrgyzstan lies further north beyond Tajikistan and has no Afghan frontier, and Azerbaijan is in the South Caucasus, west of the Caspian Sea, with no common border at all.

items.value: Statements 1, 2 and 4 — monazite is a rare-earth source, contains thorium, and only government bodies may process or export it; but it does not occur along the entire Indian coast
items.reasoning: Monazite is a rare-earth phosphate mineral and India's principal rare-earth ore, and it characteristically carries thorium, which is why it underpins the country's three-stage nuclear programme — statements 1 and 2 hold. Statement 4 is correct because monazite is a 'prescribed substance' under the Atomic Energy Act, 1962; private parties may mine other beach-sand minerals but monazite handling, processing and export are reserved to government entities such as Indian Rare Earths Ltd. Statement 3 is the false one: monazite-bearing placer sands are concentrated in specific stretches of Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh, not spread along the entire coastline.

items.value: The second half of the month of June
items.reasoning: The longest day in the northern hemisphere falls on the June solstice, when the sun is overhead at the Tropic of Cancer and the northern hemisphere is tilted maximally towards it. That date is 20-22 June, which lies in the second half of the month. The July options confuse the longest day with the hottest period, which lags the solstice by several weeks because of the thermal inertia of land and ocean.

items.value: Only two pairs are correctly matched — Renuka (Himachal Pradesh) and Rudrasagar (Tripura); Hokera is in Jammu and Kashmir and Sasthamkotta is in Kerala
items.reasoning: Renuka Wetland is in Sirmaur district of Himachal Pradesh and Rudrasagar Lake is in Tripura, so pairs 2 and 3 are right. Pair 1 is wrong: Hokera (Hokersar) is a Ramsar wetland on the outskirts of Srinagar in Jammu and Kashmir, not Punjab. Pair 4 is wrong: Sasthamkotta Lake, the largest freshwater lake in Kerala, lies in Kollam district, not Tamil Nadu. That leaves exactly two correct pairs.

items.value: All four — Aarogya Setu, CoWIN, DigiLocker and DIKSHA are built on open-source digital platforms
items.reasoning: All four are part of India's digital public infrastructure and were developed on open-source stacks with their code placed in the public domain: DIKSHA runs on the Sunbird platform, DigiLocker's code base has been opened, CoWIN's underlying certification and registration components were released for reuse by other countries, and the Aarogya Setu source code was published in 2020. Marked MED rather than HIGH because 'built on top of open-source platforms' is a claim about the underlying stack rather than a documented statutory fact, and Aarogya Setu's opening came after launch.

items.value: All three — Web 3.0 gives users control of their own data, permits blockchain-based social networks, and is collectively operated by users rather than a corporation
items.reasoning: The defining idea of Web 3.0 is decentralisation: identity and data are held by the user in wallets and distributed ledgers rather than in a company's servers, which is statement 1. Blockchain-based social platforms are a live application of exactly that model, so statement 2 holds. Statement 3 restates the same principle from the governance side — ownership and decision-making are distributed among users and token-holders instead of resting with a single corporate intermediary, the contrast with the Web 2.0 platform economy.

items.value: All three — SaaS buyers can configure the interface and data fields, users can reach their data from mobile devices, and web mail services such as Outlook, Hotmail and Yahoo! Mail are SaaS
items.reasoning: SaaS vendors routinely allow tenants to configure the look of the interface and to add or alter data fields without touching the underlying code, which is what distinguishes configuration in a multi-tenant product from bespoke software — statement 1 holds. Statement 2 follows from the delivery model: the application and data sit on the provider's cloud and are reached over the network, so any browser-capable device including a phone can access them. Statement 3 is correct, as browser-delivered mail is the textbook consumer example of software delivered as a service. MED because statement 1's customisation claim is the one a strict reader could contest.

items.value: A missile is put into a stable orbit around the Earth and then deorbited over its target
items.reasoning: A Fractional Orbital Bombardment System places a warhead into a low Earth orbit and brings it down on the target before completing a full revolution — hence 'fractional'. Its military attraction is that the weapon need not follow a predictable ballistic arc and can approach from an unexpected direction, defeating early-warning radars oriented along the shortest polar path. The other options describe asteroid deflection, a planetary lander and a comet rendezvous mission, none of which involve a weapon delivered from orbit.

items.value: Quantum Computing
items.reasoning: A qubit, or quantum bit, is the basic unit of quantum information. Unlike a classical bit that must be either 0 or 1, a qubit can exist in a superposition of both states and can be entangled with other qubits, which is the source of the parallelism that quantum computers exploit. The term has no role in cloud services, visible light communication or ordinary wireless technologies, which all handle classical bits.

items.value: All three — closed-circuit television, RFID and wireless LAN are all classed as short-range devices/technologies
items.reasoning: In radio-regulatory usage a short-range device is a low-power transmitter with limited range and low interference potential, and the ITU's own categorisation of short-range radiocommunication devices covers wireless video applications including CCTV, radio frequency identification, and radio local area networks. All three operate over metres to at most a few hundred metres, unlike cellular or satellite links. Marked MED because 'short range' is being used here as a defined regulatory category rather than in its everyday sense, and CCTV is the least obvious member of it.

items.value: All three — biofilms form on medical implants inside tissue, form on food and food-processing surfaces, and can exhibit antibiotic resistance
items.reasoning: A biofilm is a community of microbes encased in a self-produced polymeric matrix that adheres to a surface. Implanted catheters, prosthetic joints and heart valves are classic colonisation sites and a major cause of device-associated infection, so statement 1 holds. Food contact surfaces and processing equipment are equally favourable substrates, giving statement 2. Statement 3 is correct and is the clinical reason biofilms matter: the matrix impedes antibiotic penetration and the slow-growing cells inside tolerate drugs at concentrations that would kill the same organism free-floating, so biofilm infections are markedly harder to clear.

items.value: Statements 1 and 3 — probiotics include both bacteria and yeasts and help digest milk sugars; but the organisms in them do occur naturally in the human gut
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: alongside bacterial genera such as Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium, the yeast Saccharomyces boulardii is a well-established probiotic. Statement 3 is correct because lactic acid bacteria produce enzymes that break down lactose, which is why fermented dairy is better tolerated by people with lactose intolerance. Statement 2 is the false one — the whole rationale for probiotics is that they are organisms of the kind that already inhabit a healthy gut, being supplied in order to restore or reinforce that resident flora.

items.value: Statements 2 and 3 — Sputnik V is a viral-vector vaccine and COVAXIN is an inactivated-pathogen vaccine; Covishield is not an mRNA vaccine
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is wrong: Covishield, made by the Serum Institute under licence from Oxford-AstraZeneca, uses a replication-deficient chimpanzee adenovirus vector carrying the spike gene — a viral-vector platform, not mRNA. Statement 2 is correct, Sputnik V being a two-dose regimen using two different human adenoviral vectors, Ad26 and Ad5. Statement 3 is correct: COVAXIN, developed by Bharat Biotech with ICMR-NIV, is a whole-virion inactivated SARS-CoV-2 vaccine with an adjuvant.

items.value: Effects 1, 3, 4, 6 and 7 — GPS failure, power grid damage, intense auroras, disturbed satellite orbits and polar shortwave radio blackouts; tsunamis and forest fires are not solar-storm effects
items.reasoning: A severe geomagnetic storm disrupts the ionosphere through which GPS signals travel (1), induces damaging currents in long power transmission lines (3), drives spectacular auroras to much lower latitudes than usual (4), heats and expands the upper atmosphere so that satellite drag increases and orbits decay (6), and causes polar-cap absorption events that black out HF radio for aircraft on polar routes (7). Statements 2 and 5 are the invented distractors: tsunamis are generated by submarine earthquakes and landslides, and forest fires by heat, drought and ignition sources at the surface — neither is produced by solar flares.

items.value: A database created by a coalition of research organisations
items.reasoning: The Climate Action Tracker is an independent scientific project run jointly by two non-governmental research bodies, Climate Analytics and the NewClimate Institute, which track national pledges and policies against the Paris temperature goals and rate them. Its independence from the UN process is the point of it, so it is neither a wing of the IPCC nor a committee under the UNFCCC, and it is not an agency financed by UNEP and the World Bank.

items.value: Statements 1, 3 and 4 only — the Climate Group is a network-building non-profit, EP100 is about energy-efficiency innovation and competitiveness, and Indian companies are members; but EP100 was not launched with the IEA and the IEA is not the Under2 Coalition secretariat
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: The Climate Group is an international non-profit whose method is precisely to build and run corporate and sub-national networks — RE100, EP100, EV100 and the Under2 Coalition. Statement 3 restates EP100's own remit and is correct, and statement 4 is correct since several Indian companies, including cement and manufacturing majors, are EP100 members. Statement 2 is wrong because EP100 was launched by The Climate Group in partnership with the Alliance to Save Energy, not the International Energy Agency. Statement 5 is wrong because The Climate Group itself, not the IEA, serves as secretariat to the Under2 Coalition.

items.value: Aquatic plants absorb heavy metals and excess nutrients
items.reasoning: The kidney metaphor is about filtration and purification — removing waste and toxins from the fluid passing through. Of the four options only D describes that function: wetland vegetation takes up heavy metals and surplus nitrogen and phosphorus, cleansing the water before it moves on. Option A describes the hydrological cycle, B describes the food web and productivity, and C describes sediment trapping and soil stabilisation; each is a genuine wetland service but none of them is a purification function.

items.value: Statements 1 and 4 only — the WHO 2021 guideline values for PM2.5 are 15 µg/m³ over 24 hours and 5 µg/m³ annually, and ozone can trigger asthma; ozone peaks in sunny not inclement weather, and it is PM2.5 rather than PM10 that crosses into the bloodstream
items.reasoning: Statement 1 matches the revised WHO Global Air Quality Guidelines of 2021 exactly. Statement 4 is correct, ozone being a respiratory irritant that inflames the airways and provokes asthma attacks. Statement 2 is wrong: ground-level ozone is photochemically produced, so its highest concentrations occur in hot, sunny, stagnant conditions, the opposite of inclement weather. Statement 3 is wrong because the size threshold matters — PM10 is deposited in the airways, whereas it is the finer PM2.5 that penetrates the alveolar barrier and enters the bloodstream, which is why the guideline is stricter for it.

items.value: Statements 1 and 2 — Gucchi is a fungus that grows in some Himalayan forest areas; it is not commercially cultivated in the north-eastern Himalayan foothills
items.reasoning: Gucchi is the morel mushroom, Morchella species, so statement 1 is correct in calling it a fungus. Statement 2 is correct: it fruits naturally in temperate conifer and broadleaf forests of the western Himalaya, particularly Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir and Uttarakhand. Statement 3 is wrong on both counts — morels resist commercial cultivation and are gathered from the wild by forest communities, which is exactly why they command such high prices, and the harvesting region is the western rather than the north-eastern Himalaya.

items.value: Statements 1 and 3 — PET fibre is blended with wool and cotton, and PET bottles are recyclable; it is not suitable for storing any and every alcoholic beverage, and burning it does emit greenhouse gases
items.reasoning: Statement 1 is correct: polyester fibre is routinely blended with cotton and wool to add strength, crease resistance and durability. Statement 3 is correct, PET being among the most widely recycled plastics, reprocessed into fibre, sheet and fresh containers. Statement 2 overreaches with the word 'any' — PET is not accepted as a container for the full range of alcoholic beverages, high-alcohol spirits in particular raising migration and shelf-life concerns. Statement 4 is plainly wrong, since PET is a hydrocarbon polymer and its incineration necessarily releases carbon dioxide along with other pollutants.

items.value: Golden Mahseer, which is a fish
items.reasoning: The Golden Mahseer, Tor putitora, is a large freshwater cyprinid of Himalayan rivers, prized as a game fish and listed as endangered — it is not a bird. The Indian Nightjar is a nocturnal insectivorous bird, and the Spoonbill and the White Ibis are both long-legged wading birds of the family Threskiornithidae found in Indian wetlands.

items.value: Alfalfa, chickpea and clover only — all three are legumes; amaranth, purslane and spinach are not nitrogen fixers
items.reasoning: Biological nitrogen fixation in crops comes from the symbiosis between legumes and Rhizobium bacteria housed in root nodules. Alfalfa, chickpea and clover are all Fabaceae and nodulate, so 1, 3 and 4 are nitrogen-fixing. Amaranth and purslane (kulfa) belong to the Amaranthaceae and Portulacaceae, and spinach also to the Amaranthaceae; none of them forms rhizobial nodules, so they draw nitrogen from the soil rather than fixing it from the air.

items.value: Restoration of damaged coral reefs
items.reasoning: Biorock, or mineral accretion technology, passes a low-voltage direct current through a steel frame submerged in sea water, causing dissolved calcium carbonate to precipitate onto the structure. Coral fragments transplanted onto this limestone-coated frame settle and grow faster and survive stress better, which is why the method is used to rehabilitate degraded reefs, including at sites off the Gujarat coast. It has nothing to do with plant-residue building materials, shale gas prospecting or salt licks.

items.value: Creation of mini forests in urban areas
items.reasoning: The Miyawaki method, devised by the Japanese botanist Akira Miyawaki, plants native species densely on prepared soil so that they compete for light and grow rapidly into a multi-layered, self-sustaining stand in a fraction of the usual time. Because it works on plots as small as a few hundred square metres, it has been widely adopted by Indian cities to create pocket or mini forests. It is not a technique for arid-zone commercial farming, genetically modified gardens or wind energy.
